outcomes.text: Explain why new business ideas come about: changing technology, changing consumer wants, obsolete products.
Explain how new ideas arise from original ideas or by adapting existing ones.
Explain the risks (failure, loss, insecurity) and rewards (success, profit, independence) of business.
Explain the purpose of business activity: producing goods or services, meeting needs, adding value.
Describe how entrepreneurs organise resources, make decisions and take risks.
Describe customer needs: price, quality, choice and convenience.
Explain why understanding customers matters for sales and survival.
Explain why businesses do market research.
Compare primary and secondary research methods.
Explain the use of qualitative and quantitative data, social media and reliability in market research.
Identify market segments by location, demographics, lifestyle, income and age.
Use market mapping to find gaps in the market and competition.
Assess competitors' strengths and weaknesses on price, quality, location, range and service.
Explain how competition affects business decisions.

topics.title: Topic 1.3 Putting a business idea into practice

outcomes.text: Define business aims and objectives.
Distinguish financial and non-financial start-up aims and objectives.
Explain why aims and objectives differ between businesses.
Calculate revenue, fixed, variable and total costs, profit or loss, and interest.
Calculate break-even output and margin of safety.
Interpret break-even diagrams and the effect of changing revenue and costs.
Explain why cash matters and how it differs from profit.
Calculate and interpret cash-flow forecasts: inflows, outflows, net cash flow and balances.
Describe short-term sources: overdraft and trade credit.
Describe long-term sources: savings, venture capital, share capital, loans, retained profit and crowd funding.
Explain limited and unlimited liability and what they mean for owners.
Compare sole trader, partnership and private limited company ownership.
Evaluate franchising.
Explain factors in choosing a location: market, labour, materials, competitors and business nature.
Explain the impact of the internet on e-commerce versus fixed premises.
Explain price, product, promotion and place and their importance.
Explain how to balance the mix against competition, changing needs and technology.
Describe what a business plan contains.
Explain how a plan minimises risk and helps obtain finance.

topics.title: Topic 1.5 Understanding external influences on business

outcomes.text: Identify stakeholders and their objectives.
Explain how stakeholders and businesses affect each other and how their interests may conflict.
Describe e-commerce, social media, digital communication and payment systems.
Explain how technology influences sales, costs and the marketing mix.
Explain the purpose of consumer and employment law.
Explain the cost and consequences of meeting or not meeting legal obligations.
Explain how unemployment, consumer income, inflation, interest rates, taxation and exchange rates affect businesses.
Explain how a business may respond to changes in technology, legislation and the economy.
Describe internal (organic) growth by new products and new markets.
Describe external growth by merger and takeover.
Explain public limited company ownership.
Compare internal and external finance for growing businesses.

subtopics.title: Changes in business aims and objectives

outcomes.text: Explain why aims change in response to market conditions, technology, performance, legislation and internal reasons.
Describe how aims change as businesses evolve.
Explain the impact of imports, exports, changing locations and multinationals.
Describe tariffs and trade blocs as trade barriers.
Explain how businesses compete internationally using the internet and the marketing mix.
Explain trade-offs between ethics and profit.
Explain trade-offs between the environment, sustainability and profit.
Explain how pressure groups can affect the marketing mix.
Explain the design mix: function, aesthetics and cost.
Describe the product life cycle and extension strategies.
Explain why differentiating a product matters.
Describe pricing strategies.
Explain influences on pricing: technology, competition, segments and life cycle.
Choose promotion strategies for different segments.
Explain the use of technology in promotion.
Describe distribution through retailers and e-tailers.

subtopics.title: Using the marketing mix to make business decisions

outcomes.text: Explain how each element of the mix influences the others.
Explain how an integrated mix builds competitive advantage.
Explain the purpose of operations: producing goods and services.
Compare job, batch and flow production.
Explain how technology affects production: cost, productivity, quality and flexibility.
Interpret bar gate stock graphs and explain just-in-time stock control.
Explain procurement and supplier relationships.
Explain the impact of logistics and supply decisions on costs, reputation and satisfaction.
Explain quality control and quality assurance in goods and services.
Explain how quality helps control costs and gain competitive advantage.
Describe the sales process: product knowledge, speed, engagement, feedback and after-sales service.
Explain why good customer service matters.
Calculate gross profit and net profit.
Calculate and interpret gross profit margin, net profit margin and average rate of return.
Use graphs, charts, financial, marketing and market data to support business decisions.
Explain the uses and limitations of financial information.
Compare hierarchical and flat, and centralised and decentralised structures.
Explain the importance of effective communication and its barriers.
Compare part-time, full-time, flexible, permanent, temporary and freelance working and the effect of technology.
Describe key job roles and responsibilities.
Describe recruitment documents and internal and external recruitment methods.
Describe formal, informal, self-learning and ongoing training, target setting and reviews.
Explain the link between training, motivation and retention, and retraining for technology.
Explain why motivation matters: attracting, retaining and productivity.
Compare financial and non-financial motivation methods.
